transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

What scared me enough to come in is… at work, during the quiet stretches in the surveillance room, I’ve been hearing voices through the monitor speakers. They’ll say things like, “You missed it, Ruth,” or, “People are going to get hurt because of you.”

But the thing is, the channels are muted. And no one else hears it. It’s been really frightening.
Do the voices you hear ever tell you to do something?

Not exactly like commands, no. It’s more like they accuse me or warn me—like, “You missed it, Ruth,” or, “People are going to get hurt because of you.” I hear it through the monitor speakers when everything is muted, and no one else seems to hear anything.
Do you hear the voices only when you're in the surveillance room or do you hear them at other times and places as well?

So far it’s really been in the surveillance room, during those quiet stretches. I hear it like it’s coming through the monitor speakers, even when the channels are muted. I haven’t really noticed it happening other places.
Do you find that your mood changes frequently or unexpectedly?
I’m not sure I’d say it changes suddenly. I haven’t really noticed quick swings like that. Mostly I just feel kind of stuck in the same low place.
Do you believe the accusations or warnings the voices give you are true?

Part of me does believe them, yes. I keep going back over every camera angle I missed or any call I made late, and it feels like proof that I’m careless… dangerous, even. And if something goes wrong on my watch, I feel like I’d deserve to be punished for it.
Have you experienced periods where you felt extremely low or depressed for a long time?

Yes. Most days it feels like I wake up with this heavy gray mood already on me, before I even get out of bed. It’s been going on a while. Sometimes I’ll be sitting in my car before a shift and just seeing the casino lights makes me tear up, for no real reason.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely high or unusually energetic?
No, I don’t think so. I can’t remember a time where I felt unusually high or full of energy like that. If anything, my energy’s been low.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely irritable?
I don’t think I’ve had a whole period like that, no. I get frustrated sometimes, but not extremely irritable or like it took over for days.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or on top of the world?
No, not really. I can’t think of a time where I felt on top of the world or unusually happy like that.
Do you think the beliefs about being careless or dangerous, as the voices suggest, are true even when others tell you otherwise?

Yes… a lot of the time I do. Even if someone tells me I’m not careless, I keep going back over every camera angle I missed or any call I made late, and it feels like proof that I’m dangerous at my job. Part of me really believes that if something goes wrong while I’m on watch, I deserve to be punished for it.
Has your low mood made it hard for you to do your daily activities or work?

Yes. It’s made work harder. I’ve already made mistakes on shift paperwork, and I’ve had to kind of pull back from activities and seeing friends because I just can’t keep up like I used to.

At home I’m mostly just doing the basics. I’m not really cooking much, or having people over, or getting to projects I used to take care of.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually confident or optimistic?
No, I don’t think so. I’ve had times where I tried to tell myself things would be okay, but not where I felt unusually confident or optimistic.
Have you ever had a period where you didn't need much sleep and still felt rested?
No, I don’t think so. If I don’t sleep much, I usually feel worn down, not rested or energized.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually energetic and didn't need much sleep?
No, I haven’t had a time like that. If I’m not sleeping, I don’t feel energetic—I just feel tired.
Have you ever had a period where your low mood significantly improved, even if only for a little while?

Not really. Most days it’s like this heavy gray feeling is there before I even get out of bed. Sometimes I’ll be driving to my shift and just seeing the casino lights makes me tear up, and there’s not even a clear reason. It doesn’t lift much.
Does your low mood ever get better for more than a day at a time?

No, not really more than a day. Most days that heavy gray mood is there before I even get out of bed. Sometimes even just seeing the casino lights before my shift can make me tear up for no real reason.
Do you think there's any possibility that the voices and your beliefs about being careless might not be based in reality?

I don’t know. Part of me can hear what you’re saying, that maybe it could be my mind making it worse. But when I think about work, I keep replaying every missed camera angle or any delayed call, and it feels like proof that I’m careless… like I’m dangerous. And if something goes wrong on my watch, part of me really believes I deserve to be punished for it.
How long have you been feeling this heavy gray mood that you described?
It’s been about four months now. It started around when I got moved into the lead surveillance role at the casino.
Have the voices you've been hearing ever stopped for a period of time, such as a few weeks, since they started?

No, not for weeks. They started during this same stretch where I’ve been feeling so hopeless and guilty after the lead change. Before that, I never heard accusations through the equipment or felt so sure I was dangerous to everyone. It all seems tied together with this low period.
Do you think the voices and the feelings of being careless or dangerous would go away if your low mood and heavy gray feeling improved?

I think they might, yes. I mean, before this whole stretch of feeling hopeless and guilty after I got moved into the lead role, I never heard accusations through the equipment. I didn’t feel so sure I was dangerous to everyone either. So it feels like the voices and those thoughts are part of the same low period.
